source_verification_receipts.version: arXiv preprint corresponding to Journal of Econometrics 210 (2019), 459-481
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper develops second-order asymptotics for maps with a null first derivative and analyzes standard-bootstrap failure in that setting.

The paper proves exact p-value/type-I-error control and nominal-or-better confidence coverage for continuous multinomial functionals, while proposing a consistent Monte Carlo implementation because exact computation is generally difficult.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Promote the aggregate signed-cancellation theorem into the headline and exhibit a concrete coefficient array where all pairwise shifts persist but their signed aggregate shift vanishes; this makes the aggregate object independently memorable.

Add a computational complexity and practical-size analysis for the rational outer algorithm, or replace its enormous global grid certificate with an adaptive certified subdivision that retains the same coverage and diameter guarantee.
Extend the split-sample construction to overlapping original blocks through an explicit dependency-graph or compound-Poisson theorem, connecting the result to the actual unsplit panel design.

recommended_next_step: Advance to Stage 0 with the common-cutoff mixed-coefficient question as the analytic kernel and preserve the product-Poisson and certified-inference branches as independent theorem targets.
